items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-02-03
items.q: No, I didn't know him. No, I didn't never see him.

ctx.x: Did you know Stink's brother Bill Johnson? No, I didn't know him.
No, I didn't know him. No, I didn't never see him. He played banjo and face.
Yeah, that's right. What was his name?

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: Yeah, that's the one I knew, Bill Johnson.

ctx.x: He died in 1954, I believe, up in Portland at his brother's place. I made some records of him about 15 years ago. What was his brother's name now? I can't remember, it was Bill Johnson, the namesplayer. Bill Johnson, I believe. This is another brother, I can't think of his name now.
Yeah, that's the one I knew, Bill Johnson. They had another brother.

Yeah, and there was another one that played guitar or something. That's right, that's right. But I only met Bill and the Dink. And Dink. Dink died just in 54. Yeah. Was he old? Born in 92, so he was eight years older than you.
